snippet.title: Bob Ryan Knew Larry Bird Was Done After His Final Game 🥹
snippet.description:
Bob Ryan was at Richfield Coliseum in Cleveland for Larry Bird's final game, a Sunday-afternoon Game 7, and he had a feeling after the game that Bird was done. Bob and Gary Tanguay look back at the fall of the Celtics dynasty: the 57-win 1988 team, the Bird-Dominique Wilkins Game 7 duel (Bird scored 34, 20 of them in the fourth quarter; Wilkins scored 47; Celtics 118, Hawks 116), Kevin McHale's greatness (.604 from the field and .797 from the line in 1987-88), the Ainge trade, Reggie Lewis's emergence and the end of the Big Three.

Plus: is Jayson Tatum a legitimate MVP candidate? Mitchell Robinson and the Celtics' frontcourt questions, the 76ers' hot start with LeBron James as the "Swiss Army knife," and Jaylen Brown saying it's Tyrese Maxey's team.

snippet.title: 1988 Celtics vs Knicks: When Larry  Bird Ended Ewing's First Playoff Run
snippet.description:
Larry Bird vs. Patrick Ewing, 1988: both wore No. 33. Bird was 31 and chasing his fourth title. Ewing was 25 and playing in his first playoff series. Four games in the 1988 first round, with the archival tape and the box scores. Nick Gelso breaks down the Celtics-Knicks series through the two men wearing 33.

The numbers (Basketball-Reference): Bird averaged 28.3 points, 5.8 rebounds and 8.0 assists on 48% shooting. Ewing averaged 18.8 points and 12.8 rebounds and blocked 13 shots. Boston won the series, 3-1, with Game 3 the Knicks' only win (109-100).

Game 1, April 29, Celtics 112, Knicks 92: Bird had 29 points on 11-of-12 at the line, and Ewing blocked five shots. Game 2, May 1, Celtics 128, Knicks 102: Bird had 36 points, and Ewing had 18 points, 10 rebounds, 6 steals and 3 blocks. Game 3, May 4, Knicks 109, Celtics 100: Ewing had 31 points on 10-of-16 shooting, and Bird shot 8-of-22 but had 20 points, 12 assists and 5 steals. Game 4, May 6, Celtics 102, Knicks 94: Bird had 28 points, and Ewing shot 3-of-12 but had 20 rebounds.

snippet.title: The Lakers Coach Magic Got Fired 😳 Bob Ryan Explains
snippet.description:
Bob Ryan and Gary Tanguay on the Bob Ryan & Jeff Goodman Podcast: why did Magic Johnson refuse to play for Paul Westhead? Ryan tells the story: Jack McKinney's bicycle accident, Westhead taking over the Lakers, the clash over Showtime tempo vs. Kareem's low-post game, and Magic winning the battle "with the owner rather than the coach." Then Westhead's 1990-91 Denver Nuggets, which Ryan calls the craziest team in NBA history.

The numbers (Basketball-Reference): the 1990-91 Nuggets led the NBA in scoring at 119.9 points a game and allowed 130.8, an NBA record. They gave up 100 or more in all 82 games. Westhead won the 1980 NBA title with the Lakers, was fired 11 games into the 1981-82 season, and Pat Riley took over. In June 2026 Westhead received the NBCA's Chuck Daly Lifetime Achievement Award.

snippet.description:
Bob Ryan and Gary Tanguay on the Bob Ryan & Jeff Goodman Podcast: Wilt Chamberlain, one of the most underappreciated players in NBA history. Ryan breaks down Wilt's three-phase career, why his numbers read like science fiction, Wilt vs. Bill Russell (a rivalry Ryan ranks above Bird vs. Magic), the 1967 76ers who ended the Celtics' run, Wilt vs. Shaq, and whether Russell let Wilt pad his stats.

The numbers (Basketball-Reference): 100 points on March 2, 1962. 50.4 points a game in 1961-62. 55 rebounds against Russell's Celtics on Nov. 24, 1960. On April 11, 1967, Wilt had 29 points, 36 rebounds and 13 assists as the 76ers beat Boston 140-116 in Game 5 of the Eastern Division finals.

snippet.title: Why Larry Bird Shot Better With Goggles He Hated | The 1988 Tapes 📼
snippet.description:
Another entry from the CLNS archive vault — March 15, 1988, Market Square Arena, and Larry Bird is playing with a fractured orbital bone and a pair of goggles he couldn't stand.

snippet.title: Jordan vs. Bird: 1988 Duel No One Remembers | The 1988 Tapes 📼
snippet.description:
Another entry from the CLNS archive vault — January 12, 1988, Chicago Stadium, and the Bird-Jordan duel almost nobody brings up. Maybe bc it wasn’t in the playoffs? Maybe bc time just skipped over it. Either way, CLNS The Tapes series is dustin off the vhs and breaking this one down.. 

Larry Bird went for 38 points, 9 rebounds and 8 assists in 44 minutes. Michael Jordan answered with 42 on 19-of-35. Both men had exactly 10 points at halftime. Then they combined for 60 after the break.

But the number nobody talks about is zero.

With 23 seconds left, the Chicago Stadium PA announcer called Michael Jordan for his sixth personal foul and sent him to the bench. The foul belonged to Charles Oakley. Jordan finished the night with ZERO personal fouls and ZERO turnovers in 43 minutes — and re-entered the game with two seconds on the clock.

Also on this tape: Kevin McHale's 10,000th career point, Danny Ainge extending his three-point streak record on a 1-for-5 night, Robert Parish going 18 and 16, a rookie Reggie Lewis, Fred Roberts wearing Cedric Maxwell's number 31, and Ric Flair and Dusty Rhodes sitting courtside in fur coats.

Boston won 104-97. Twenty-five days later both teams were back in this same building for All-Star Weekend. Two rounds apart that spring, Detroit ended both their seasons.
